annotations.title: Repenting him.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Note how ſpedily the plague of God falleth after ſinne, and ſpecially men muſt note what torment of conſcience, and deſperation often foloweth the ſheading of innocent bloud.

annotations.title: Hung him ſelf.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> If he had rightly repented, notwithſtanding his horrible treaſon, he might haue obteyned mercy: but by hanging him ſelf he tooke away al meanes of mercy and ſaluation, becauſe he died finally impenitent.

annotations.title: Innocent of his bloud.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Though Pilate was much more innocent then the Iewes, and would haue been free from the murder of our Sauiour, ſeeking al the meanes that he could (without offending the people and the Emperours lawes) to dimiſſe him: Yet he is damned for being the miniſter of the peoples wicked wil againſt his owne conſcience. euen as al Officers be, and ſpecially the Iudges and Iuries which execute lawes of temporal Princes againſt Catholike men: for al ſuch be guilty of innocent bloud, and be nothing excuſed by that they execute other mens will according to the lawes, which be vniuſt. For they ſhould rather ſuffer death them ſelues, then put an innocent man to death.

notes.text: They that execute lawes against their conscience, are like to Pilate.

annotations.title: If thou be the Sonne.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Maruel not, when thou heareſt our Sauiour in the B. Sacrament mocked at, or ſeeſt him abuſed of wicked men, that he ſtraight reuengeth not ſuch blaſphemies: or that he ſheweth not him ſelf there viſibly and to the ſenſes, when faithles Heretikes wil ſay, Let me ſee him, taſt him, &c. for he ſuffered here the like on the Croſſe, when he might at his will haue come downe with as much eaſe as he roſe when he was dead.

notes.text: Christ derided in the B. Sacrament, euen as vpon the Crosse.

annotations.title: Why haſt thou forſaken me.
annotations.text: Beware here of the deteſtable blaſphemie of Caluin and the Caluiniſts, [1]who thinking not the bodily death of Chriſt ſufficient, ſay, that he was alſo here ſo forſaken and abandoned of his Father, that he ſuſtained in ſoule and conſcience the very feares and torments of the damned. And to take away the Article of his deſcending into Hel after his death, (which was [2]with triumph and not in paine,) they ſay that his deſcending was nothing els, but that his ſoule ſuffered the very paines of Hel vpon the Croſſe. Whereas in deede by theſe wordes out of the Pſalme, our Sauiour wil ſignifie no more but that his paines (being now ſo long on the Croſſe and ready to die) were very great, and therfore according to the infirmity of his humane nature, for very anguiſh (as before in the garden when he was but toward his Paſſion) he ſaith he was forſaken, for two cauſes, firſt becauſe it was the wil of God not to deliuer him, but that he ſhould die: ſecondly, becauſe his diuine nature did ſo repreſſe it ſelf for the time, that he felt no comfort thereof at al, but was left to die in extreme paines as a mere man.

notes.text: Detestable blasphemy of Calvin. And other Ministers of his school.

annotations.title: Wrapped.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> This honour and duty done to Chriſtes body being dead, was maruelous grateful and meritorious. And this wrapping of it in cleane ſindon may ſignifie by S. Hierom, <mn>[2]</mn>that the Body of our Lord is to be wrapped not in gold, pretious ſtones, and ſilke, but in pure linnen. And ſo in the whole Church it is obſerued by <mn>[3]</mn> S. Silueſters conſtitution, that the Corporal <mn>[4]</mn> whereupon our Lordes body lieth on the altar, muſt be pure and plaine linnen.

notes.text: Reuerent vsing of our L. Body.
